catalog_quote: (The existence of lexical tone on Dadiya nouns is easily established by citing pairs of nouns that contrast in meaning based only on carrying different tones.) [...] Every member of both subject index sets has a tone, either H or L, linked to it. [...] So at least in all paradigms presented here, the tone on the verb is not lexical (tied to the verb's dictionary meaning) but grammatical (determined by the aspect it conveys). [...] Here is a minimal pair of Dadiya imperative forms contrasting only in tone: dʊ́wá 'Carry!'; dʊ̀wà 'Flex!' (Randy Groff, p.c.).

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Saved file opened: title page 'Stephen Dettweiler 2021-12-15, (c) 2021 SIL Nigeria', Introduction 'Dadiya [dbd] is an Adamawa language spoken in northeastern Nigeria'. All four quoted fragments found verbatim at A's locators: txt l.169-170 (sec. 4, '(The existence of lexical tone on Dadiya nouns is easily established by citing pairs of nouns that contrast in meaning based only on carrying different tones.)'), l.228 (sec. 5 first sentence 'Every member of both subject index sets has a tone, either H or L, linked to it.'), l.704-705 (sec. 8, p.13 'the tone on the verb is not lexical.. but grammatical (determined by the aspect it conveys)'), l.246 (fn.6 minimal pair dʊ́wá 'Carry!' / dʊ̀wà 'Fle…
new_statements.relation_note: Tone only (H/L, downstep, lexical vs grammatical tone, orthographic tone marking); vowel inventory with ATR in Appendix 2; no mention of stress/accent.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Dadiya is tonal: two tone levels (H, L) with automatic and non-automatic downstep of H; lexical tone is contrastive on nouns (minimal pairs) and at least some verbs (dʊ́wá 'carry!' vs dʊ̀wà 'flex!'), while tone melodies on the verb word mark aspect (progressive/perfective: tone spreads from the subject index; future: H on verb; habitual: L on verb). Nothing is said about word stress or accent anywhere in the paper (full-text search: 'stress' 0, 'accent' only in 'acute accent diacritic').
new_statements.secondary_stress: not discussed (no stress discussed at all)
new_statements.exceptions: Author flags the analysis as preliminary: whether verbs carry lexical tone in addition to grammatical tone is unresolved (Type 1 vs Type 2 verb melodies; clause-initial verbs show either lexical tone or default L); phrase-initial H is heard as medium pitch (also reported for Waja, Kleinewillinghöfer 2020); downstepped H does not reset within the phrase.
new_statements.identity_note: Explicitly Dadiya [dbd], Adamawa, NE Nigeria where Gombe/Taraba/Adamawa meet; speakers from the Dadiya translation team (Bambam area); data include 'gólá Lódíyá' (Lodiya road). Same work as Glottolog ref 675151 / our works still to obtain 'Dettweiler 2021 Notes on Dadiya Verbs and Tone' (previously 'not located'). Title page carries 'SELF-REVIEWED DRAFT ONLY - CIRCULATED FOR COMMENT - SEEK AUTHOR'S PERMISSION BEFORE CITING', though SIL has archived it publicly 'as is'.
